Following the release of the seventh developer beta versions of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and Apple's other upcoming software updates, Apple is now rolling out the corresponding public beta versions. Here are the details.

Apple Releases New Public Beta Versions

Earlier, Apple released:

  • iOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate Developer Beta 7 (Build: 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24R5358a)

Apple is now rolling out the corresponding versions for the public beta, marking the fifth round of public beta releases. To date, Apple has released new public beta versions for iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's release does not include any particularly notable changes, as Apple is now primarily focused on bug fixes and stability improvements in preparation for the official launch expected in a few weeks.

In addition, Apple has also released the second public RC of macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20), following the earlier release of the corresponding developer RC. The second RC of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is also expected to be released soon, as it has already been released at 7:42 PM Eastern Time.

Among all of today's releases, the public beta build numbers are exactly the same as their corresponding developer versions.

Sign Up for the Apple Public Beta Program

To register your device for the public beta program, please visit https://beta.apple.com and follow the steps for each respective device. Here's how to install the public beta on your iPhone:

  • Visit the Apple Beta Software Program website, then choose to register or sign in.
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone, then accept the program's terms and register your account.
  • Open "Settings" on your iPhone.
  • Go to "General" > "Software Update" > "Beta Updates".
  • Select iOS 27 Public Beta.
  • Return to the "Software Update" page, then tap "Update Now" when the beta version appears.

Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you are using your primary iPhone, be sure to make a recent backup beforehand.

Have you discovered any changes in this beta? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
